grant_type.description: Always `authorization_code`: this request exchanges the code from the authorize redirect for tokens. Any other value — `refresh_token` included — is `unsupported_grant_type`, refused before the code is looked up.

code.description: The authorization code from the redirect. It may be exchanged once; a second presentation is `invalid_grant`, the same answer a fabricated code gets.

redirect_uri.description: The same redirect URI the authorize request used. It is compared, not merely recorded.

client_id.description: The client making the exchange, as registered.

code_verifier.description: The PKCE verifier whose `S256` hash was sent as the challenge at the authorize step. Between `43` and `128` unreserved characters, per RFC 7636 §4.1 — it is compared rather than parsed, so a length nobody checks is a length an attacker chooses. PKCE is mandatory for every client under OAuth 2.1.

resource.description: The resource the token is requested for, per RFC 8707. It must match the audience the code was authorized for, or the answer is `invalid_target`; omitted, the code's own audience stands. It becomes the token's `aud`, and a resource refuses a token whose audience names something else — which is what keeps a token minted for one app out of another app's endpoint.

description: RFC 6749 §4.1.3's authorization-code exchange with PKCE, as either MCP authorization server reads it. Sent as `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, per §4.1.3, though the server accepts a JSON body too.
